_meta.name: Lard Soap (Piggie Soap / Grandma's Lye Soap)
_meta.source_note: a.k.a. Piggie Soap, Grandma's Lye Soap. Attributed to Deanna.
_meta.altitude_note: Cold-process soap chemistry is not altitude-sensitive. No adjustment needed at 9,000 ft.
_meta.family_baseline_note: Not a food recipe — serving baseline not applicable.

servings.yield_note: ~20 oz per lb-batch (~4-5 bars at 4.5 oz each)

steps.title: Gear up
steps.content: Before anything else: rubber gloves, safety goggles, clothes you can ruin. Set up in the sink or lay down several layers of newspaper. Lye is caustic — treat it with respect.

steps.title: Melt the lard
steps.content: Melt lard in a saucepan over medium-low heat until fully liquid. Remove from heat.

steps.title: Mix the lye water
steps.content: Weigh water into a pitcher. Slowly sprinkle lye INTO the water — lye into water, never the other way. Gently swirl to dissolve. The mixture will heat up; this is normal.

steps.title: Cool both to touch
steps.content: Let both containers cool until you can touch the outside without burning yourself. Don't rush — if either is too hot, the soap can seize or separate.

steps.title: Blend to trace
steps.content: Pour the lye water into the saucepan. Use an immersion blender — work in the sink or over newspaper. Blend until trace: drips stay visible on the surface for 1-2 seconds before sinking back in. This takes a while with lard.

steps.title: Pour into mold
steps.content: Pour into Pringles can(s) or milk carton(s). One lb-batch fills roughly one standard Pringles can — handy for shave-cup-sized bars.

steps.title: Unmold and slice
steps.content: Let sit 1-2 days at room temp. Peel off the container and slice into bars. Average store bar is 4.5 oz — cut to your preference.

steps.title: Cure
steps.content: Set bars somewhere cool and dry. Cure for 3 full weeks before use. Don't skip the cure — the lye is still finishing its work.

notes: All amounts BY WEIGHT — use a kitchen scale, not measuring cups, especially for water and lye. Lye into water always — never water into lye. Yield: ~20 oz per lb-batch (~4-5 bars at 4.5 oz). Pringles can mold makes shave-cup-sized bars. PQ: evaluate whether household consumable recipes need a separate library from food recipes (Chow Hall Layer 3 scope).
